title: Session billing and reimbursement calculation
problem: Art therapists in private practice must calculate session fees, insurance reimbursements, sliding scale adjustments, and track unpaid balances manually. Errors lead to revenue loss or client disputes. Many use spreadsheets or mental math, wasting time each billing cycle.
who: Private practice art therapists handling their own billing

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Session Billing Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates session fees, insurance reimbursements, sliding scale rates, and monthly revenue projections for art therapy private practice
skill_spec.formula_hint: gross = session_rate * sessions_per_week * 4.33; insurance = insured_sessions * rate * reimbursement_pct; sliding_loss = sliding_clients * rate * discount_pct * 4.33; no_show_loss = gross * no_show_rate

example_queries: Calculate my monthly revenue if I charge $150/session, see 20 clients a week, and insurance reimburses 70%
How much am I losing with 5 sliding scale clients at 40% discount and a 12% no-show rate?

title: Supervised practice hours tracking for credentialing
problem: Art therapists pursuing ATR or ATR-BC credentials must track hundreds of supervised practice hours across multiple categories (direct client contact, supervision hours, accredited vs non-accredited program requirements). Miscounting delays credentialing by months and costs application fees.
who: ATR-P provisional art therapists working toward full registration

skill_spec.name: ATCB Credential Hours Tracker
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates remaining supervised practice and supervision hours needed for ATR and ATR-BC credentials based on ATCB 2025-2026 standards

inputs.name: atr_bc_supervision_hours
inputs.label: Hours supervised by ATR-BC or ATCS

skill_spec.formula_hint: Accredited: 1000 direct + 100 supervision (50 from ATR-BC/ATCS); Non-accredited: 1000 direct + 150 supervision (75 from ATR-BC/ATCS); weeks = max(remaining_direct / weekly_hours, remaining_supervision / weekly_supervision_rate)

example_queries: I graduated from a CAAHEP-accredited program, have 650 direct hours and 60 supervision hours. How much more do I need for ATR?
How many weeks until I can apply for ATR-BC if I'm doing 25 client hours per week?

title: SOAP clinical note writing for art therapy sessions
problem: Art therapists must write detailed SOAP notes after every session, documenting client behavior, art process observations, clinical interpretations, and treatment progress. This documentation takes 15-30 minutes per client and must meet HIPAA and insurance audit standards. Poor notes lead to denied insurance claims.
who: All practicing art therapists, especially those billing insurance

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy SOAP Note Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates structured SOAP clinical notes for art therapy sessions with art-specific observations and medical necessity language

variables.name: art_process_observations
variables.label: Observations of art-making process (colors, pressure, engagement)

skill_spec.structure_hint: S: Client statements, mood, self-report -> O: Art medium, process observations, behavioral observations, artwork description -> A: Clinical interpretation, progress toward treatment goals, medical necessity -> P: Next session plan, interventions to continue/modify, referrals

example_queries: Write a SOAP note for a session where my client used watercolors to explore grief, was tearful but engaged
Generate a progress note for a group art therapy session with 6 adolescents working on self-esteem through collage

title: State licensing requirements lookup
problem: Art therapy licensing varies dramatically across 20+ states - some require ATR-BC, others accept related licenses, some only offer title protection. Therapists relocating or seeking telehealth clients across state lines waste hours researching requirements and risk practicing without proper credentials.
who: Art therapists relocating, pursuing telehealth, or advising students

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy State Licensing Guide
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of art therapy licensing requirements, credential recognition, and scope of practice by state (2025-2026 data)
skill_spec.data_domain: State-by-state art therapy licensing requirements, credential types, and regulatory bodies

data_hints.source_law: State practice acts and ATCB requirements

example_queries: What are the licensing requirements for art therapists in New York?
Can I practice art therapy via telehealth with clients in Texas if I'm licensed in Connecticut?
Which states accept ATR-BC as sufficient for licensure without additional state exams?

title: HIPAA compliance checklist for private practice
problem: Private practice art therapists must comply with HIPAA but many use non-compliant tools to reduce costs. They risk $100-$50,000+ fines per violation. Many don't know what constitutes a violation - storing client artwork photos on personal phones, using regular Zoom instead of HIPAA-compliant platforms, or emailing client information without encryption.
who: Art therapists in private practice, especially solo practitioners

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy HIPAA Compliance Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step HIPAA compliance audit for art therapy private practice covering digital records, artwork storage, telehealth, and communication
steps: Step 1: Verify EHR system has signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
Step 2: Confirm telehealth platform is HIPAA-compliant (e.g., Doxy.me, not regular Zoom)
Step 3: Review client artwork photo storage - must be on encrypted, BAA-covered platform, not personal phone
Step 4: Check email encryption for any client communications containing PHI
Step 5: Verify physical artwork storage is in locked location with access controls
Step 6: Review intake forms for required Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgment
Step 7: Confirm all staff/contractors have signed confidentiality agreements
Step 8: Check that client records retention policy meets state requirements (typically 7 years)
Step 9: Verify breach notification procedures are documented
Step 10: Review and update Security Risk Assessment annually
warnings: Warning: Storing client artwork photos on personal devices without encryption violates HIPAA
Warning: Using free video platforms without BAA for telehealth sessions is a HIPAA violation
Warning: HIPAA fines range from $100 to $50,000 per violation, up to $1.5M annually per category

example_queries: Is it a HIPAA violation to photograph client artwork with my personal phone?
What do I need to check to make sure my private practice is HIPAA compliant?
Can I use Google Drive to store client session notes?

title: Treatment plan development from assessment
problem: Art therapists must create individualized treatment plans that align with DSM-5 diagnoses, include measurable goals, specify art-based interventions, and satisfy insurance requirements for medical necessity. Writing a comprehensive plan takes 1-2 hours per client and must be updated regularly.
who: All clinical art therapists, especially those new to practice

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Treatment Plan Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates individualized art therapy treatment plans with DSM-5 aligned goals, art-based interventions, and medical necessity documentation
skill_spec.structure_hint: Client demographics -> Diagnosis & presenting concerns -> Measurable treatment goals (SMART format) -> Art therapy interventions matched to goals -> Session frequency & duration -> Progress measurement criteria -> Review schedule -> Medical necessity justification

example_queries: Create a treatment plan for a 10-year-old with anxiety disorder using art therapy interventions
Generate a treatment plan for an adult trauma survivor, DSM-5 309.81, for weekly outpatient art therapy

title: ICD-10 and CPT code lookup for art therapy billing
problem: Art therapists billing insurance must use correct ICD-10 diagnostic codes and CPT procedure codes, but art therapy doesn't have its own CPT codes and must bill under psychotherapy codes. Using wrong codes leads to claim denials. Different insurers accept different code combinations, creating confusion.
who: Art therapists billing insurance, especially in private practice

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Billing Code Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of ICD-10 diagnostic codes and CPT procedure codes commonly used for art therapy insurance billing
skill_spec.data_domain: ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes and CPT psychotherapy codes applicable to art therapy sessions

data_hints.source_law: AMA CPT Code Set, WHO ICD-10-CM

example_queries: What CPT code do I use for a 50-minute individual art therapy session?
Which ICD-10 codes are commonly paired with art therapy for anxiety in children?
Can I bill CPT 90837 for a 60-minute art therapy session?

title: Art supply budget and inventory management
problem: Art therapists must maintain diverse art supplies across multiple media (paints, clay, markers, paper, collage materials, etc.). They struggle to track inventory, budget for replenishment, and justify material costs to employers or for tax deductions. Running out of supplies mid-session disrupts therapeutic work.
who: Art therapists managing their own supply budgets in any setting

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Supply Budget Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates monthly and annual art supply costs based on client volume, media types used, and session frequency

inputs.name: group_sessions_per_week
inputs.label: Number of group sessions per week

inputs.name: media_types
inputs.label: Art media used (paint, clay, drawing, collage, mixed media)

outputs.name: cost_per_client_session
outputs.label: Average supply cost per client session (USD)

outputs.name: tax_deductible_amount
outputs.label: Potential tax-deductible amount (USD) for private practice

skill_spec.formula_hint: Base per-session cost by media type (paint=$5, clay=$4, drawing=$2, collage=$3, mixed=$6); total = (individual_sessions + group_sessions * group_size) * weighted_media_cost * 4.33; tax_deduction = total if private practice (Schedule C)

example_queries: How much should I budget for art supplies if I see 18 individual clients and run 3 groups of 6 per week?
What's the per-session cost of supplies if I mainly use painting and clay?

title: Insurance credentialing and panel application
problem: Art therapists seeking insurance reimbursement must navigate complex credentialing processes with each insurance company. Many insurers don't recognize art therapists as providers, requiring them to credential under mental health counselor or psychotherapy categories. Missing steps delays revenue by months.
who: Art therapists in private practice seeking insurance panel acceptance

skill_spec.name: Insurance Credentialing Checklist for Art Therapists
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step guide for art therapists to apply for insurance panel credentialing, including required documents and common pitfalls
steps: Step 1: Verify your state license type is accepted by target insurer (check if art therapy is recognized vs. mental health counselor category)
Step 2: Obtain NPI (National Provider Identifier) number if not already registered
Step 3: Register with CAQH ProView and complete provider profile
Step 4: Gather required documents: license, ATR-BC certificate, malpractice insurance, DEA (if applicable), diplomas, CV
Step 5: Submit credentialing application to each insurance panel individually
Step 6: Follow up every 2 weeks - average processing time is 90-120 days
Step 7: Once approved, verify your listing in provider directory is correct
Step 8: Set up electronic claims submission through your EHR or clearinghouse
Step 9: Submit test claim and verify payment within 30 days
Step 10: Calendar re-credentialing dates (typically every 2-3 years)
warnings: Warning: Some states do not recognize art therapists as independent mental health providers for insurance purposes
Warning: Billing for services before credentialing is complete may not be retroactively reimbursed
Warning: Each insurer has different taxonomy codes - verify correct code for art therapy

example_queries: How do I get credentialed with Blue Cross Blue Shield as an art therapist?
What documents do I need to apply for insurance panels?
How long does insurance credentialing typically take for art therapists?

title: Continuing education requirements tracking
problem: Art therapists must complete continuing education hours to maintain ATR-BC certification and state licenses, but requirements differ between ATCB and each state. Tracking CE credits across multiple providers and ensuring they meet specific category requirements (ethics, cultural competency, supervision) is confusing and time-consuming.
who: ATR-BC certified art therapists maintaining credentials

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy CE Requirements Tracker
skill_spec.one_liner: Tracks continuing education progress against ATCB and state-specific requirements with category breakdowns and deadline reminders
steps: Step 1: Identify your renewal cycle dates for ATCB credential and state license
Step 2: List total CE hours required (ATCB: 100 hours per 5-year cycle for ATR-BC)
Step 3: Check state-specific additional requirements (ethics hours, cultural competency, etc.)
Step 4: Log completed CE hours by category and provider
Step 5: Verify CE provider is approved by ATCB or state board
Step 6: Calculate remaining hours needed by category
Step 7: Check for overlap - some CEs satisfy both ATCB and state requirements
Step 8: Calendar deadline reminders 90 days before renewal
Step 9: Gather certificates of completion for submission
Step 10: Submit renewal application with documentation before deadline
warnings: Warning: Lapsed ATR-BC requires additional fees and potentially retaking the board exam
Warning: Not all online CE courses are ATCB-approved - verify before purchasing
Warning: Some states require specific ethics hours that general CEs don't satisfy

example_queries: How many CE hours do I need to renew my ATR-BC?
Do AATA conference sessions count toward my state CE requirements?
My ATR-BC renewal is in 6 months and I have 45 of 100 hours. What categories should I focus on?

title: Scope of practice compliance by state
problem: Art therapists face scope of practice conflicts - some states restrict them from conducting assessments or diagnoses despite their clinical training. Practicing outside scope risks license revocation and legal liability. The rules change frequently with new legislation in multiple states.
who: Art therapists practicing in states with restrictive scope of practice laws

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Scope of Practice Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Advises art therapists on what clinical activities are within their scope of practice by state, including assessment, diagnosis, and independent practice
skill_spec.expertise_area: Art therapy scope of practice regulations, state-by-state clinical activity permissions

example_queries: Can I conduct psychological assessments as an art therapist in Connecticut under the new proposed scope changes?
Am I allowed to diagnose clients independently as a licensed art therapist in New York?
What happens if I'm hired as a recreation therapist at a VA hospital but I'm trained as an art therapist?

title: Client intake and informed consent documentation
problem: Art therapists need comprehensive intake forms that cover both standard mental health intake AND art therapy-specific consent (use of artwork, photography of art, artwork ownership/storage). Missing art-specific consent elements creates legal liability. Templates from generic therapy practices don't include these elements.
who: Art therapists starting private practice or updating intake procedures

skill_spec.name: Art Therapy Intake & Consent Form Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates customized intake forms and informed consent documents with art therapy-specific clauses for artwork use, storage, and confidentiality
skill_spec.doc_name: Art Therapy Informed Consent and Intake Form

variables.name: artwork_policy
variables.label: Artwork retention policy (client keeps / therapist retains / shared)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Practice information -> Therapist credentials & license -> Nature of art therapy (explanation) -> Confidentiality & HIPAA notice -> Artwork ownership & storage consent -> Permission to photograph artwork -> Telehealth consent (if applicable) -> Fees & cancellation policy -> Emergency procedures -> Client rights -> Signatures

example_queries: Generate an informed consent form for my art therapy private practice in Maryland that includes artwork photography consent
Create intake paperwork for a children's art therapy practice that parents need to sign
